key_insight: The paper argues that isotropic turbulence can be viewed as an SO(3) gauge theory in which symmetry breaking splits the flow into a smooth cascade sector and a confined vortex-filament sector.
engineering_relevance: If valid, this framework could offer a new physics-based way to interpret, model, and potentially control coherent vortex structures in high-Re turbulence.
method: Map angular momentum to an SO(3) gauge connection and radial velocity to a Higgs field.
Use spontaneous symmetry breaking SO(3)→U(1) to separate massless cascade modes from massive filament modes.
Validate the theory against DNS via spectra, vortex-core profiles, and Wilson-loop statistics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with JHTDB DNS at Re_λ≈433, including a 1:2 spectral equipartition, BPS-like vortex-core profiles, and an area-law Wilson loop.
watch_item: The interpretation is highly theoretical and depends on strong analogies to gauge-field physics, so independent replication and sensitivity checks are essential before using it as a turbulence model.
paper_title: An SO(3) Gauge Theory of Turbulence with Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
